# Independent audit: all-dimensional simplex facet convex order

Audited the complete source `candidate 8e69e6820cd6ee00`.



## 1. Radial laws and convex order

For an `(m-1)`-simplex with `m>=2`, the radial cone parametrization from a fixed vertex has independent opposite-facet direction and radial density `(m-1)r^(m-2)`. Tilting uniform volume by `m lambda_j=m(1-r)` gives exactly `m(m-1)r^(m-2)(1-r)`, whose mass is one and mean is `(m-1)/(m+1)`. Contracting the uniform radial variable by `alpha=m/(m+1)` gives density `(m-1)alpha^(-(m-1))r^(m-2)` on `[0,alpha]`, with the same mass and mean.

Their difference has the asserted signs `+,-,+`: the interior crossing is `q=1-alpha^(-(m-1))/m`; Bernoulli gives `m alpha^(m-1)>=2m/(m+1)>1`, so `q>0`. At `alpha`, the inside bracket is `alpha-alpha^(-(m-1))<0`, and outside the contracted support the tilted density is positive. Thus `q<alpha`.

For a continuous convex test on the radial interval, subtracting its secant through `q,alpha` gives nonnegative values outside and nonpositive values inside. Multiplying by the density difference therefore gives a nonnegative integral; the affine part vanishes by equal mass and first moment. This is the correct convex-order direction. Conditioning on the same opposite-facet point preserves convexity in the radial coordinate, and averaging the tilted measures gives uniform volume because their densities average to `sum lambda_j=1`.

The degenerate `m=1` case is explicitly handled as a point. No undefined Beta distribution is used there. The case `m=2` has a one-point opposite facet and otherwise the same one-dimensional proof.

## 2. Actual facet normalization

On a facet of a `d`-simplex, there are exactly `m=d` remaining barycentric vertices. Each captured facet piece is `alpha F+(1-alpha)v_j`, with Jacobian `alpha^(d-1)`, where `alpha=d/(d+1)`. Its contribution to the profile has weight `1/(d+1)`. Applying the mixture inequality therefore gives coefficient

    d alpha^(d-1)/(d+1)=alpha^d=Gamma_d.

Equivalently the normalized density `W/Gamma_d` is precisely the uniform mixture of those contracted facet laws. This checks the distinction between the ambient simplex dimension and the facet dimension, which is essential here.

For `d=1`, facets are individual endpoints carrying `H_0`; the profile at each is `1/2=Gamma_1`, so the proof does not invoke a zero-dimensional cone density. For `d>=2`, shared lower-dimensional facet intersections have zero surface measure. Different facet areas and fixed outward normals cause no missing Jacobians, since the inequality holds on each facet separately with its own measure. Normal-dependent potentials are covered whenever their physical restriction at each fixed normal is convex.

## 3. Mixed product, criticality and sharpness

The affine Hamming function is zero at its chosen binary base and at least one at every other measured base. Since a barycentric coordinate is at most one, the associated caps strictly miss all other fibers by a margin at least `1/(d+1)`. Their own cap volume is `Gamma_d |K|`; differentiating `(1-t)^d|K|` gives the common positive coarea measure `d alpha^(d-1)|K|`. Their balanced circuit therefore has equal response weights, and the centroid of every own section has all barycentric coordinates equal to `1/(d+1)`.

These are proper cuts on their own full-dimensional fiber and strict empty cuts elsewhere. Hence their regular boundary-profile interpretation has no coincident supporting-facet allocation. The upper bound for global depth follows from the cap cover of each own fiber. The lower bound at a fiber centroid follows from the separately proved ordinary simplex centroid theorem, including oblique ambient cuts through restriction to that actual fiber. Pure-integer containing caps include the whole own fiber and cannot lower the bound.

For every admissible nonnegative potential, summing the separate facet inequalities gives the common upper bound `Gamma_d/N`. The explicit base hinges attain individual efficiency `Gamma_d` and sum to one on every measured base, so their sum attains the common bound. All denominator and attainment claims are thus exact; no maximizer compactness is invoked. The result includes `n=0`, `d=1`, and closed caps, while correctly excluding `d=0` from this boundary-measure argument.

No unresolved step was found. The new assertion is the exact whole-cone potential optimum, rather than a new proof of unrestricted OC.
